question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)=(2 y)\,i+(- 2 x + 3 y)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(- 3 t - 3)\,i+(- 2 t + 3)\,j$ for $t\in[0,1].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 3 t - 3,\quad y=- 2 t + 3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(2 y)\,i+(- 2 x + 3 y)\,j \\  & =(- 4 t + 6)\,i+(15)\,j \\  & =(- 4 t + 6)\,i+(15)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t - 3)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t + 3)\,j \\  & =(-3)\,i+(-2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) & =((- 4 t + 6)\,i+(15)\,j)\cdot((-3)\,i+(-2)\,j) \\  & =(- 4 t + 6)\cdot(-3)+(15)\cdot(-2) \\  & =(12 t - 18)+(-30) \\  & =12 t - 48\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r & =\int_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int_{0}^{1}(12 t - 48)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\left[6 t^{2} - 48 t\right]_{0}^{1} \\  & =((-48)+(6))-((0)+(0)) \\  & =(-42)-(0) \\  & =-42\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(\frac{- 2 y - 2}{x})\,i+(\frac{4 x - 4}{y})\,j \\  & =(- \frac{2}{t})\,i+(\frac{4 t^{2} - 4}{t - 1})\,j \\  & =(- \frac{2}{t})\,i+(4 t + 4)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t - 1)\,j \\  & =(2 t)\,i+(1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) & =((- \frac{2}{t})\,i+(4 t + 4)\,j)\cdot((2 t)\,i+(1)\,j) \\  & =(- \frac{2}{t})\cdot(2 t)+(4 t + 4)\cdot(1) \\  & =(-4)+(4 t + 4) \\  & =4 t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r & =\int_{3}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int_{3}^{4}(4 t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\left[2 t^{2}\right]_{3}^{4} \\  & =((32))-((18)) \\  & =(32)-(18) \\  & =14\end{aligned}
